- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via DatasourceSchema (symbol, a top-level const), ROUTE_SHADOWED_DATASOURCE_NAMES (symbol, a top-level const object), /api/v1/datasources (route, a path literal in routeShadowedNameRefusal), /api/v1/datasources/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line; a path literal in reason; a path literal in routeShadowedNameRefusal), /api/v1/datasources/drivers (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line; a path literal in reason), /datasources/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via DatasourceSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/datasources (route, a path literal in routeShadowedNameRefusal), /api/v1/datasources/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line; a path literal in reason; a path literal in routeShadowedNameRefusal), /datasources/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-service.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 96fb7b5d07afaf828f4c0de4ba0fe3d179984e86` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ce6a2047d6ea13af52afd5a827beaa7a591f84e8` — the merge of head `e5f6120b7f55592da59b6e9d2b7f710fe25be6a8` into base `96fb7b5d07afaf828f4c0de4ba0fe3d179984e86`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ce6a2047d6ea13af52afd5a827beaa7a591f84e8 && git checkout ce6a2047d6ea13af52afd5a827beaa7a591f84e8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 96fb7b5d07afaf828f4c0de4ba0fe3d179984e86 e5f6120b7f55592da59b6e9d2b7f710fe25be6a8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 96fb7b5d07afaf828f4c0de4ba0fe3d179984e86 && git merge --no-ff e5f6120b7f55592da59b6e9d2b7f710fe25be6a8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 96fb7b5d07afaf828f4c0de4ba0fe3d179984e86
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 96fb7b5d07afaf828f4c0de4ba0fe3d179984e86` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 待裁：新公开名字 `ROUTE_SHADOWED_DATASOURCE_NAMES`（#29308）

- 一句话问题：名叫 `drivers` 的数据源能保存，但管理接口 `GET /api/v1/datasources/drivers` 被驱动目录路由抢走，这个数据源永远无法按名字读到。这个 PR 让 spec 拒收这类名字。被保留的名字放在一个新的公开导出常量里，路由也从它挂载，名字需要您定。
- 背景：分诊 6576569136 定"保留集取自一个导出常量，路由也从它挂载"；席位定由 spec 持有，`service-datasource` 引用它。
- 选项：
  - A 保留 `ROUTE_SHADOWED_DATASOURCE_NAMES`（冻结数组 `['drivers']`）：零额外工作，名字直说原因：被路由遮住的数据源名。
  - B 改名（例如 `RESERVED_DATASOURCE_NAMES`）：更短，但不说明为什么保留。改名要重新生成 api-surface/export-origins 并出复审 delta，约半小时。
- 附带一问（开发 Q2）：`service-datasource` 的 `DRIVER_CATALOG_SEGMENT` 按这个数组做类型约束（A，已实现），而不是 spec 再导出第二个常量（B）。推荐 A，少一个公开名字。
- 推荐：两问都是 A。盲区：将来若有第二条遮名路由，数组会变长，名字仍然成立。
- 自检：只看①选 A；②③④ 是否翻转：否。
- 落地：在此卡标签取下前，席位不挂自动合并。

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4df813f3ea788b1ac5904d651a2271bff8dde85f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/datasource.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.datasource-name-route-shadowed-refused.ts + packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-route-reserved-names.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-service.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/admin-routes.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/__tests__/datasource-route-reserved-names.test.ts, packages/spec/src/data/datasource-route-shadowed-name.test.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save-door-refusals.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.stack-datasource-host-reserved-name-refused.ts, packages/spec/scripts/build-migration-registry.ts, .changeset/29308-datasource-route-shadowed-name.md

Inputs read: card #29308 (body, triage 6576569136, claim 6578377666, os-dev-report 6579884811), PR #29423 (body, 9-file list, net diff against merge-base `eef116e4` of `main`), the check-runs on the head (two polls), the live tree at the head via `git show`. The remainder of the diff (the test file, the docs, the regenerated references, the changeset, the service-datasource re-export) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT; it is READ here to judge the two `hits` files, not reviewed.

Check-runs on the head at the second poll: 0 failures. Green: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, Lint (CI/release/engine gates, ESLint, docs & code guards, repo & tooling gates, PM dispatch-gates, scoped x3), Type Check (source gates, debt ledger), Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs, Check PR Size. Still in_progress: Build Core, Test Core (shards 3-8), Test UI (1-16), Type Check (workspace, consumer gates, UI). The landing rule (AGENTS.md #14, Tier S) needs every check green independently of this record; nothing read here predicts a red.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged against the live tree:

1. `DatasourceSchema.name` refuses `drivers` (one `invalid_format` issue at `name`), via a second `.regex()` with a negative lookahead built from `ROUTE_SHADOWED_DATASOURCE_NAMES`. RIGHT. The first pattern (`^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$`) still fires first for off-pattern input, so `Drivers` meets the identifier refusal and not this one (pinned as a control). Negative-lookahead patterns are established spec practice (`flow.zod.ts:623`, `override-declaration.zod.ts:62`, `datasource.zod.ts:181`), so no portability rule is broken.
2. Every door that parses `DatasourceSchema` inherits the refusal: `defineDatasource` (`datasource.zod.ts:1019`, parses the schema), a stack's `datasources` (`stack.zod.ts:695`, `z.array(DatasourceSchema)`), and the metadata save door (`metadata-type-schemas.ts:131` maps `datasource` to `DatasourceSchema`; `protocol-save-door-refusals.ts:454/522` turn a failed parse into `422 INVALID_METADATA`). RIGHT; the PR body's "every door" claim holds in the cited code.
3. The published JSON Schema carries the refusal as a second `pattern` (zod 4 `allOf`), so JSON-Schema consumers refuse the name too. RIGHT, and pinned by the new test; no `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` row is owed because a `.regex()` check is not a refinement.
4. `default` stays accepted by `DatasourceSchema` and stays refused only on the stack collection (`stack.zod.ts:643-660`); `test` stays accepted. RIGHT (both pinned as controls); the constant's docblock states why `default` is not in the list, matching the stack file's own rule.
5. The admin create door (`datasource-admin-service.ts:818-819`) runs `assertValidName` before any schema parse and refuses `drivers` with its own 400 sentence; no double refusal. RIGHT; the door pins are unchanged and green per the report.
6. A stored `drivers` row at the admin PATCH door: a `label`/`active`-only edit is spared (`RECORD_JUDGE_EXEMPT_PATCH_KEYS`, `:930-940`); an edit touching `config`/`driver`/`pool`/`external` or carrying a secret now meets `assertValidRecord` and the spec's sentence. RIGHT as a derived narrowing on the PATCH door, correctly named in the PR body and the out_of_scope note; same posture as every other spec refusal on a stored row.

Public-surface changes:

7. New export `ROUTE_SHADOWED_DATASOURCE_NAMES` (`Object.freeze(['drivers'] as const)`, type `readonly ['drivers']`) from `@objectstack/spec/data` (`data/index.ts:302` re-exports the module); `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` carry it. RIGHT. It is a new public name and so needs the maintainer's nod (③).
8. `@objectstack/service-datasource`: `ROUTE_SHADOWED_DATASOURCE_NAMES` keeps its declared type `readonly string[]` and is now the spec's array; `DRIVER_CATALOG_SEGMENT` is typed `(typeof SPEC_...)[number]`, i.e. `'drivers'`, so the registrar (`admin-routes.ts:696`) mounts the catalog from a member of the spec list and a segment the spec does not reserve does not compile. RIGHT: one list, both halves, and the drift pin (`__tests__/datasource-route-reserved-names.test.ts:80`) still compares the list to the literals actually mounted beside a same-method `/:name`, in both directions.
9. `DatasourceSchema.name`'s `describe` text changes, so `content/docs/references/data/datasource.mdx` is regenerated; the text in the mdx is byte-identical to the describe string. RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/29308-datasource-route-shadowed-name.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/service-datasource: patch`. RIGHT. The kind is `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` (a value refused), which grades at least one moved package `minor`+ (spec, where the narrowing is); service-datasource's published source moves (it imports the spec list) and the narrowing is not its own, so `patch` is the honest level; Check Changeset is green on the head, LEVEL AXIS accounted. The changeset body carries both declaration lines, a BREAKING banner, the FROM → TO remedy (rename, re-point `datasource`/`datasourceMapping`), and exactly one marker `adr-0087: registered datasource-name-route-shadowed-refused`, whose id matches the entry's `id:` line (the gate's id regex at `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs:2073`). PR title carries `fix(spec)!:`.

`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset, matched by `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. RIGHT. The pair admits one arm; the diff narrows a published accept set, which is the ADR-0087 breaking signal, and the additive public export is carried by the `minor` level rather than a `yes` arm (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, level axis: `Clause-②` keeps its meaning and loses its level coupling; a `narrowed` kind cannot sit beside a line without `(narrowing)`). The delta anticipated the question ("if the export gate reads `yes`, follow the gate"); the gate read it as accepted.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (os-dev-report 6579884811):

- open_questions 1, the export name `ROUTE_SHADOWED_DATASOURCE_NAMES` (A) vs `RESERVED_DATASOURCE_NAMES` (B). Judgment: A is right; B would read as if `default` belonged in it, and `default` must keep parsing. ESCALATED: a new public name needs the maintainer's approval before landing (standard order §5; the PR body's 需要你做的 says so). The seat asks; this record does not stand in for that nod.
- open_questions 2, `DRIVER_CATALOG_SEGMENT` as a typed literal rather than an index into the tuple. ANSWERED: A suffices. The type binds the segment to the spec list at compile time, and the unchanged drift pin binds the list to the mounted routes at test time; a second public name would add nothing enforced.
- deviations[0], `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx` outside the claim's surface. ANSWERED: the claim comment 6578377666 already names that sentence in its file surface ("amended on the dev's report"); nothing to split.
- deviations[1], service-datasource `patch`. ANSWERED in ②.
- deviations[2] and [3] (no MCP writes, no PR-activity subscription). Procedural, consistent with the standing order; nothing to judge.
- out_of_scope_findings (a stored `drivers` row can no longer take a config/driver/pool/external edit at the admin door). Read and agreed: the expected posture of a spec refusal on a stored row; the PR body documents it; no carrier owed.

Reviewer's own check, asked by the brief: does any `ui/**` mirror of `DatasourceSchema` drop the new name refusal (the objectui#7715 class)? NO. `git grep DatasourceSchema` under `ui/` at the head finds only direct imports from `@objectstack/spec/data` (tests in `app-shell`), prose, and the parity test that lists `DatasourceSchema` as a name the spec owns and ui never mirrors (`ui/packages/types/src/__tests__/report-chart-query-spec-parity.test.ts:742`). There is no derived zod twin to drop the check. The Console's datasource page has a client-side convenience gate (`DatasourceResourcePage.tsx:491`, the identifier regex alone), which lets `drivers` reach the server, where the create door's 400 sentence comes back as the save-failed toast; that is the author's words rendered, not a silent accept, and it is not a schema mirror. No finding on this PR.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/data/datasource.zod.ts`, against the ruling (seat's call on the card: the reservation lives in the spec, from one exported constant the routes also mount from) and its first consumers (`service-datasource` registrar and create door; the metadata save door; `stack.zod.ts`):

- Holds. One frozen constant beside the schema; the registrar's catalog segment is typed against it and the create door's membership test reads it; the drift pin keeps the list equal to the mounted literals in both directions; `DatasourceSchema.name` refuses each entry with one issue at `name`, which the save door turns into `422 INVALID_METADATA` and `defineStack` into `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` at `datasources.N.name` (pinned). The host's `default` row and the draft-probe literal `test` are correctly left out, with the reason stated where the next reader will look. The refusal is a pattern, so the published JSON Schema carries it and no refinement baseline moves.
- Tried to break: (i) `Drivers` or `DRIVERS` — met by the identifier pattern first, one issue, control pinned. (ii) A name containing the word (`drivers_archive`, `_drivers`, `my_drivers`) — the lookahead is anchored `^(?!(?:drivers)$)`, so they pass; pinned. (iii) A future second entry that is not a snake_case identifier would need regex escaping — the test pins every entry against the `name` pattern, so the unescaped join is safe by construction. (iv) A future literal mounted by the registrar without a reservation — the drift pin fails; a future spec entry no route shadows — the drift pin fails the other way. (v) The create door double-refusing — `assertValidName` runs first and throws; the schema is never reached for that input.
- should-fix (not a FAIL): `ROUTE_SHADOWED_NAME_REFUSAL` is one static sentence built for the WHOLE list ("Datasource name 'drivers' is reserved ... at /api/v1/datasources/drivers ..."), not for the offending input. With one entry it reads exactly right; the day a second entry lands the sentence becomes "Datasource name 'drivers', 'x' is reserved ... at /api/v1/datasources/drivers and /api/v1/datasources/x", and the per-name test (`startsWith("Datasource name '${name}' is reserved: ")`) fails on its own. zod 4's `.regex()` accepts a message FUNCTION of the issue, which can name the offending input and would keep the sentence per-name as the list grows. Cosmetic today; worth fixing while the list has one member.
- Observation, no action owed: the admin create door's own sentence ("at '/datasources/drivers'") and the spec's sentence ("at /api/v1/datasources/drivers, ahead of the by-name read ...") are two wordings of one refusal. The delta accepted "same message family" and the door's pin binds its wording, so this is recorded, not asked for. The `NAME_RE` docblock in `datasource-admin-service.ts:57` ("mirrors `DatasourceSchema.name`") now describes only the first of two patterns; `assertValidName` covers the second by the list, so nothing is dropped.

`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.datasource-name-route-shadowed-refused.ts`, against its first consumer (the ADR-0087 registry generator and the changeset marker) and its execution plan (the sibling `18.stack-datasource-host-reserved-name-refused.ts` it is modelled on):

- Holds. Shape matches `SemanticMigration` (`id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`; no `conversionIds`, since it judges no mechanical edit; no relevance question, like its sibling). The `18.` prefix is the protocol major the generator reads off the filename (`build-migration-registry.ts:200`), and spec is at 18.2.0. The id is registered by the changeset marker, and `check:adr-0087-registration` read it as "registered (new here)". The `reason` states the measured-producers count, and the `acceptanceCriteria` are a real "done when" (no issue at `name` or `datasources.N.name`; the save door answers 200 for the renamed datasource; a stored row loads `valid: false` and its next save is refused; label/active edits and removal still work), each of which the cited code and the new tests make true. "NOT mechanically convertible" is right: the new name and the objects that route to it are the author's call, exactly as the sibling says of `default`.
- Tried to break: every door the `surface` names (`defineDatasource`, a stack's `datasources`, `os validate`, `os build`, the metadata save door) reaches `DatasourceSchema` in the cited code; the claim "the one list the admin routes mount from" is true at the head (the registrar mounts from a member of the spec list). Nothing in the entry overstates the tree.
- No finding.

Must-fix: 0. Should-fix: 1 (the per-list refusal sentence).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e5f6120b7f55592da59b6e9d2b7f710fe25be6a8`
Local-runs: none

This is a DELTA record for the push after the PASS record 6580118235 (head `4df813f3`). The delta `4df813f3...e5f6120b` is one fast-forward commit across 3 files, and it is the record's Should-fix done as asked. In `packages/spec/src/data/datasource.zod.ts` the static `ROUTE_SHADOWED_NAME_REFUSAL` (one sentence for the whole list) becomes `routeShadowedNameRefusal(issue)`, passed as `.regex(NOT_ROUTE_SHADOWED_NAME, { error: routeShadowedNameRefusal })`. It builds the sentence from `issue.input`, so it names the offending name and its route only.
